feature_flags.name: FEATURE_SINGLE_SPEAKER_APPROVAL_UX
feature_flags.documented_state: PR #471; when on, run_agent() (app.py:3761-3819) treats a Gateway-owned approval-queuing turn as an early-return boundary: it does not call the Agent's LLM again and returns only the Gateway's own ApprovalLifecycleResult text for that turn
feature_flags.evidence_scope: code (app.py's PR1 single-speaker boundary) plus CHANGELOG.md PR #471 entry

notes: No class TurnCoordinator exists on main; Phase 0 TurnEnvelope instrumentation is observation-only.
route_request and handle_lead_candidate are current de-facto routing/ownership surfaces.
The coordinator consumes typed signals and must not invent business state or approval policy.

PR #471 changed who legitimately owns a turn's final reply, not just how routing is observed: when FEATURE_SINGLE_SPEAKER_APPROVAL_UX is on and this turn queued an approval, run_agent() hands the reply to the Gateway (reply_owner="gateway") and returns immediately without a further Agent turn (app.py:3761). This is a conditional, code-level ownership assignment for approval-queuing turns specifically — it does not create a general reply_owner claim mechanism and does not resolve the concurrency race (a callback and a concurrent text turn for the same identity) described in docs/architecture/turn-coordinator/REPLY_OWNERSHIP_AND_APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_RESEARCH.md §1.3c, which remains unmitigated and research-only.

The same handoff path still invokes the RP5 shadow observer (observe_shadow_finalizer, app.py:3795) on the Gateway-owned reply before returning — RP5's classification runs even though the Agent's own LLM text is never produced for that turn; see layer.rp5's notes.

edges.notes: Routing may select an approval path but cannot create approval truth.
A future decision selects a handler; execution stays downstream.
The behavior contract is blocked on the cross-layer matrix.
Turn state cannot replace approval lifecycle authority.

PR #471: the Gateway-owned approval-turn early-return path in run_agent() still invokes RP5's shadow observer before returning, so RP5 is reachable from this layer even when no Agent text is produced.
